memoryReview.lesson: Keep the same immediacy of world editing, but use a spatially continuous gas field instead of agent tiles.
Avoid the source app's camera-following 3D crash yard; place the entire shock chamber under fixed measuring instruments.
Avoid square-piece DOM puzzles and colored path trails; walls and paths must be solved from the pressure field.

references.observation: NASA explains shock discontinuities as coupled changes in density, pressure and temperature in a calorically perfect gas.
references.principle: Conserve gas mass, momentum and total energy rather than animating decorative rings.
references.application: Use the ideal-gas equation of state with gamma 1.4 and numerical conservative fluxes.
references.avoid: Do not claim detailed combustion chemistry or high-temperature real-gas equations.

references.observation: NASA shows interacting shock fronts and surfaces with different geometries of wave crossing.
references.principle: Let shape and boundary conditions change the pressure front's evolution.
references.application: Include mirrors, slits, a maze and a channel with live editable wall segments.
references.avoid: Do not copy precomputed images as a stand-in for field simulation.

references.observation: NASA describes schlieren photography as a visualization of refraction by density gradients across shock waves.
references.principle: Expose density gradients as a separate inspection visualization.
references.application: Calculate local raster density gradient for a sharp Schlieren-inspired view.
references.avoid: Do not label a direct gradient rendering a faithful optical ray tracing of schlieren optics.

concepts.medium: Real-time CPU finite-volume fluid simulation rendered through low-resolution Canvas raster and supersampled measuring marks.
concepts.composition: Dominant full viewport gas tank with fixed side instrument console and mobile bottom console.
concepts.interaction: Freehand pressure pulses, raster obstacle painting and live spot measurements directly inside the same tank.
concepts.motion: Computed compressible wavefronts move through actual conservative numerical steps; source identification fades rapidly.
concepts.rationale: Lets users create meaningful experiments with a small offline physical solver and direct manipulation.

concepts.medium: Static diagrams with separate computational previews for each educational case and a small readout.
concepts.composition: A scrollable stack of independent experiment cards around miniature fixed-width plots.
concepts.interaction: Preset selection and scalar sliders update each preselected case without freehand geometry editing.
concepts.motion: Recorded frame loops and chart transitions illustrate known shock behaviors rather than solving fluid interactions live.
concepts.rationale: Would teach fixed cases, but cannot support the user-directed open ended shock laboratory.

concepts.medium: Three-dimensional volumetric gas display rendered by heavy WebGL raymarching and preauthored meshes.
concepts.composition: Full-screen navigable flight wind tunnel with semi-transparent data volumes and diegetic controls.
concepts.interaction: The camera orbits the tunnel and draggable 3D nozzle components define inlet flow.
concepts.motion: Smoke and shader-based volumetric compression move independently from expensive three-dimensional fluid solves.
concepts.rationale: A 3D camera would sacrifice tablet legibility and exact geometry manipulation; a proper 3D solver exceeds the mobile budget.

selection.reason: A live HLL solver and immediate geometry painting are the shortest route to physically meaningful, repeatable experiments on a phone.

rejected.reason: Static cards cannot produce original reflections and refractions when the user sketches a new barrier.
A volumetric third dimension greatly increases computation while obscuring the two-dimensional shock fronts.

tools.reason: Standard Canvas 2D image raster and hand-written SVG icon work with PocketWorks Quick PWA without extra dependencies.

assets.role: A pulse trace engraved inside a radiating pressure field distinguishes the installable app.
assets.acceptance: Pulse amplitude and concentric shock rings remain legible in the mobile launcher icon.
assets.integration: Referenced directly by index.html and manifest.webmanifest and held in the owned offline cache.
assets.provenance: Author-written vector illustration with no copied art or third-party assets.

risks: The chamber may become too short on a 320px-wide phone when an in-browser safe area is tall.
Continuous numerical stepping may become CPU bound on older phones, requiring fewer adaptive grid cells.
